prompt: What is the difference between && and & for boolean expressions?
choices: && short-circuits (stops evaluation if the first operand determines the result); & always evaluates both operands
& is for bitwise AND on integers; && can only be used with booleans in conditions
&&  evaluates right to left; & evaluates left to right
explanation: && is the short-circuit AND: if the left side is false, the right side is not evaluated. & always evaluates both sides (useful if the right side has a side effect, rare in practice). Similarly: || is short-circuit OR; | always evaluates both.
